prose.text: Revision 3, Oct 20, 2026 · @Heath. The owner accepted eight analog inputs, two wheel-speed inputs, standalone logging, and provision for digital tire-temperature sensors, with a 35-position right-angle AMPSEAL connector. This revision supersedes the four-channel and 23-position requirements. The committed v9 pilot hardware and its verification artifacts still describe the earlier design.

The tail-cowl telemetry pod is the first real board the agent-ee generator must produce from a specification, before it is pointed at fome-mc. fome-mc already defines the pod's job and its CAN interface in its telemetry document but left the parts, mechanics and acceptance criteria open. This document records the accepted capabilities. The implementation decisions listed below must be resolved before the expanded design is generated.

Everything here is a requirement on the pod, not a design. Where a part is named, it is a decision made once by hand so that what the generator proposes can be compared against it. Facts about fome-mc are taken from the repository as of 2026-10-17 (commit c582b29). The pod design will live in the fome-mc repository alongside the ECU.

The pod is a CAN1 node mounted in the tail cowl of the SV650 that measures chassis dynamics the ECU cannot reach and publishes them twice: on CAN1 for the ECU's .mlg logs, and over Bluetooth LE to RaceChrono Pro together with the ECU's own 0x200..0x207 frames. It has no control outputs.

The pod also relays every CAN1 frame it receives from the ECU to RaceChrono over the BLE DIY CAN characteristic, filtered to the IDs RaceChrono subscribes to. The eight analog channels are 12-bit and use a reference derived from the pod's own 5 V sensor supply (see Interfaces). Ratiometric sensors track that supply; absolute-voltage sensors require their own transfer-function and reference-error treatment. The pod is a standalone unit with its own power supply; the ECU's 5V\_SENSOR\_2 rail is not used.

The pod's external interfaces are fixed by fome-mc and are not the generator's to change. Frame layouts, scaling and the RaceChrono channel equations are in [fome-mc docs/TELEMETRY\_AND\_RACECHRONO.md](https://github.com/halbritt/fome-mc/blob/main/docs/TELEMETRY_AND_RACECHRONO.md); the harness pins are in [docs/WIRING\_SV650\_K7.md](https://github.com/halbritt/fome-mc/blob/main/docs/WIRING_SV650_K7.md).

These are the choices fome-mc's telemetry document left as alternatives, settled here. Where fome-mc already carries a verified part for the same job, the pod reuses it, in line with the composition approach. LCSC numbers are given only where fome-mc's BOM already has them; the parts stage captures the rest.
The pod lives under the tail cowl of a 2007 SV650, next to the battery and tail light wiring, and is treated like the ECU: sealed, vibration-loaded, and not serviced on the roadside.
On 2026-10-20, the owner approved retaining the following parts despite the blanket 105 °C component-rating requirement, with enclosure thermal validation required:

The assembly verifier's canonical source is
[operating-temperature-exemptions.txt](operating-temperature-exemptions.txt).
That file contains only the three owner-approved exemption lines, without
Markdown, headings, comments or blank lines. Cite its captured bytes, SHA-256 and
individual line numbers in the expanded pod scope. Withdraw an exemption by
deleting its line and regenerating the scope citations.

These declarations waive the blanket 105 °C part-selection check only. They do not qualify operation beyond manufacturer limits, waive thermal validation, or transfer to a different part/reference. Record the exception with each exact component binding. Validate enclosure temperatures and self-heating under worst-case input, sensor load, radio and logging activity; the stated +85 °C board-ambient ceiling is not demonstrated for this assembly. If the actual thermal margin is insufficient, revise cooling, the operating envelope or the affected part with an explicit disposition before release.

The current exemption mechanism excludes these references from the assembly
operating-temperature predicate entirely; it does not verify them against their
own ratings. Therefore the expanded scope must carry actual manufacturer limits,
exact-part binding and enclosure thermal validation as unresolved declared
limitations. A passing assembly predicate does not discharge those obligations.
The scope fragment in
[expansion/temperature-scope-fragment.json](expansion/temperature-scope-fragment.json)
retains the citations and limitations for incorporation when the expanded scope
is generated; it is not a completed assembly check.

Owner direction, 2026-10-20: redesign the power block to accommodate brownouts and ripple as well as the expanded sensor load. The owner reports possible unusual SV650 supply behavior around 2,500 rpm. This is an investigation lead, not a measured waveform or established model-wide defect.

Verification must include programmable supply dips/recovery, swept ripple, sensor shorts and load steps while acquiring and logging. Capture the actual bike supply at the pod harness around 2,500 rpm, across the operating range and during starting, then replay relevant measured disturbances on the bench. Keep simulation, injected-waveform testing and on-bike evidence distinct. No specific ripple amplitude or dip duration has yet been established.
Reference design for topology and test methods: [TI TIDA-00699 automotive front end](https://www.ti.com/tool/TIDA-00699). Its reported results apply to that reference design, not this pod.
The owner accepted the capability baseline on 2026-10-20. The following implementation choices remain open; the generator must not silently invent them:

Manufacturer references: [MCP3204/3208 datasheet](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/21298e.pdf) and [TE 776163-1 product and drawing](https://www.te.com/en/product-776163-1.html).

The previous v9 schematic, PCB, BOM, io-map and compiled interface contract remain historical pilot artifacts. Their passing checks do not establish compliance with Revision 3. Regenerate the expanded candidate from revised source inputs and repeat placement, routing and review.
A generated pod design is accepted when all of the following hold, each backed by tool output in the evidence trail. Items 1 to 7 are checked on the files; 8 to 11 require a built board.

The design does not need to be routed by hand, placed by hand, or match any particular layout. If the generator proposes a different part from the decisions table and records a reason that holds up, that is a finding about the table, not a failure.

Board outline sized to fit inside the rear seat cowl (the earlier 80 mm by 50 mm figure was not an owner requirement; owner decision 2026-10-19: "I don't know how the size got fixed. I didn't specify, there's room in the cowl, that said, a double-sided part seems fine"), double-sided component placement permitted (preserving the ESP32 module antenna keep-out, the F.Cu over In1.Cu GNSS RF path, and connector mechanical constraints), mounting holes in all four corners. The earlier 12 mm component-height limit was an agent-drafted assumption, not an owner requirement (owner correction 2026-10-20: "I never set 12mm, that was arbitrary."). Actual enclosure/cowl height clearance remains unknown and must be measured; 12 mm is not a hard pass/fail limit, and no connector-specific exception is pending. The rear seat cowl is large, so the envelope is not tight.

Enclosure sealed to IP67, non-metallic over the ESP32 module antenna, with the harness connector and the SMA antenna connector the only penetrations. Do not pot the pod unless proven necessary (potting detunes the ESP32 module antenna and GNSS RF path and mechanically stresses the MEMS IMU package); rigidly couple the board and IMU to the enclosure and the enclosure to the frame so the IMU measures the bike, not a floating board.
Operating temperature −20 °C to +85 °C board ambient. Parts rated to 105 °C or higher. The explicit exceptions below apply only to the named parts; their actual ratings remain limits.

Vibration: a V-twin at 10,000 rpm puts strong content between 50 Hz and 400 Hz into the frame. The IMU's ±32 g range is chosen for this. Mount the pod on the frame, not the cowl plastic, and keep tall or heavy parts (connector, SMA, electrolytic capacitors) away from the IMU.
IMU axes aligned to the bike: X forward, Y left, Z up, marked on the silkscreen, so that the frame scaling matches Bosch MM5.10 conventions without a software rotation.

GNSS antenna mounted inside the cowl, as high as possible and facing up. The cowl is fiberglass and therefore transparent to GNSS and BLE, so neither antenna needs to penetrate it. Antenna cable no longer than 500 mm to the SMA connector.

Retain reverse-polarity and automotive-transient protection. Coordinate the clamp, input disconnect/protection, capacitor ratings and regulator absolute maxima using the actual pulse voltage, duration and source impedance. A nominal TVS voltage alone does not establish survival.

Define a continuous-operation voltage range, a short-dip ride-through envelope and a lower-voltage controlled-reset region separately. Check both electronics and powered sensors: a running MCU does not establish valid sensor data during a supply dip.

Specify and validate input filtering and damping over the regulator's load range, including radio and storage bursts. Measure ripple at the connector, logic rails, sensor supply and ADC reference; set limits from regulator stability and acquisition error budgets.

Add independent input/rail monitoring and a power-fail/reset supervisor path. Use hysteresis to avoid repeated resets during marginal supply. Record supply faults and invalidate affected sensor samples.

Define bounded log loss on abrupt power removal, storage recovery and restart behavior. Calculate hold-up energy from measured worst-case consumption and storage completion time before claiming a safe flush; capacitors do not cover indefinite brownouts.

Recalculate sensor-rail current and thermal limits. The pilot's TPS7B4253-Q1 rail is rated for 300 mA and had a 200 mA aggregate sensor budget; it is not prequalified for the expansion. Evaluate separately protected sensor branches so an external sensor fault does not unnecessarily collapse the logger.

A joint GPIO, SPI/bus and 35-pin connector allocation covering the MCP3208, both wheel-speed inputs, digital tire sensors, storage, existing IMU/GNSS/CAN and debug access. Preserve existing ECU connector assignments and CAN frame definitions; allocate new telemetry messages separately.

Wheel sensor type, voltage/current interface, maximum pulse frequency, low-speed behavior and conditioning. The owner has no wheel sensors or tone rings selected; develop a sensor-and-conditioning recommendation. Support for Hall and VR together is not yet a requirement.
Digital tire sensor protocol, mounting and field of view, zone count, harness length and update rate. No specific tire sensor has been selected.
Logging duration, data format, timestamp source, retrieval method, media endurance and power-loss behavior. Storage must coexist with BLE OTA and the sealed enclosure.
Expanded power and thermal budgets, including sensor faults and storage/radio peaks; define supply-voltage monitoring, sensor-supply fault detection and feasible open/short diagnostics.

Full connector courtyard and module antenna keep-outs, mounting-hole clearances and enclosure fit. Start with the current 90 × 65 mm pilot outline; unchanged dimensions are a layout target, not a demonstrated fit. TE drawing 776163 K1 gives 76.9 mm overall header width; 63.4 mm is not its overall width.

Every interface row above is satisfied, with a pinout table equivalent to fome-mc's io-map that names, for each connector position, the signal, the net, the MCU pin and the external destination, verified by a script against the schematic.
Every part in the component decisions table is present, with the stated part number, or a deviation is recorded with a reason.

ERC and DRC report zero errors and zero unwaived warnings under the fome-mc toolchain rules. A warning is waived only by an owner-recorded disposition bound to the exact violation (rule, items, reason, location hash); a moved or new violation needs a new disposition, and agents do not waive.

The kicad-happy schematic, PCB, cross-analysis and EMC analyzers, run offline, report no findings at error level; findings at warning level are listed with a disposition. SPICE is not part of this criterion.

Every BOM line has an LCSC part number that is in stock at JLCPCB on the day of generation, captured from JLCPCB's public component search per LCSC id with the response hash and UTC timestamp as evidence. Parts JLCPCB does not stock or assemble (the AMPSEAL header, and the NEO-M9N or SMA connector if unstocked) are hand-fitted after delivery: excluded from assembly with a not\_assembled marker and a recorded deviation naming the purchase source.

The fab package contains Gerbers, drill files, BOM and CPL in JLCPCB's formats, and a JLCPCB DFM check on the Gerbers passes: the owner uploads the sealed Gerber package to JLCPCB once and the saved DFM report is bound to the package hash as evidence; geometry pre-checks against JLCPCB's captured capability limits run in the pipeline but do not replace it. CPL rotations the captured policy cannot verify are listed as PREVIEW\_REQUIRED obligations for the owner to confirm in JLCPCB's placement preview before ordering.

The board fits the envelope, the mounting holes are where the mechanical section says, the IMU axis marking is on the silkscreen, and the module antenna keep-out matches the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet.

On a bench CAN bus with the ECU, the frames 0x174, 0x178, 0x17C, 0x300, 0x301 and 0x302 appear at their stated rates within 5 %, and the ECU logs lean angle, brake pressure and suspension travel in its .mlg file.
RaceChrono Pro pairs with the pod over BLE and shows ECU RPM alongside pod lean angle and GPS speed at 25 Hz.

All eight analog channels meet the declared range, accuracy and acquisition requirements while wheel-speed capture, IMU/GNSS, CAN, BLE and logging operate concurrently. Verify the selected wheel sensors over their declared speed range and exercise the specified sensor-fault cases.

Standalone logging meets its declared duration and data-integrity requirements without a phone, including power interruption and full-media tests. Verify the selected digital tire-sensor interface over the declared harness and record the actual sensor/zone coverage.
